prompt: An alkene is treated with Hg(OAc)₂ in ROH, then NaBH₄. What's the product?

options.label: A Markovnikov ether — RO goes on the more substituted C, no cation rearrangement
A Markovnikov alcohol — the ROH acts only as solvent; H₂O attacks instead
An epoxide — Hg(OAc)₂ oxidizes the alkene across both faces syn
An anti-Markovnikov ether — the bridged mercurinium forces attack at the less hindered C

explanation: Hg(OAc)₂ bridges the alkene (mercurinium); the alcohol (ROH, not solvent) opens it at the MORE substituted C (positive-character site). NaBH₄ removes Hg → Markovnikov ether. No free cation → no rearrangements. This is how you make 3° ethers that Williamson can't deliver (3° RX + alkoxide = E2).
